back: Ready-made application software written for many users with similar needs; bought or licensed and installed straight away.
Software written or adapted to meet the exact requirements of one organisation.
Software whose source code is freely available to study, change and share under an open-source licence.
Cheaper (cost shared by many buyers); available immediately; well tested; lots of support, tutorials and trained users.
Expensive; long development time; may have more errors at first; support only from its developers.
Support often only from community forums; changing it needs programming skills; may be less polished or compatible.
A legal agreement stating how software may be used, e.g. how many computers it may be installed on and whether it may be copied or changed.
Freeware: free to use permanently, code closed. Shareware: free trial (time- or feature-limited), then payment expected.
When the organisation's needs are specialised or unique, no package fits, and it can afford the cost and wait.
